transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-22 08:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samantha Green (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Novaflow CTO), Marcus Lee (Novaflow Head of Ops), Ellen Park (Novaflow Compliance)
Links shared: playbook deck https://redwood.app/decks/novaflow-activation-v2.pdf, pricing spreadsheet (drive) https://drive.redwood/novaflow/pricing-v3.xlsx, pilot README https://redwood.app/pilots/novaflow-readme

Auto-summary:
- Novaflow is evaluating a 12-month extension + uplift for multi-region (EU + APAC) with an EU on-prem pilot for regulated workloads.
- Primary blockers: KMS/HSM expectations, SOC2 audit evidence, latency SLO for clinical inference (p95 sub-300ms target), and contract language for data residency.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to share revised contract language and pricing; SE to run benchmarks; Novaflow to provide forecast and compliance confirmation.

Topics:
- Renewal term options and commitment sizing
- EU on-prem pilot vs VPC hosting tradeoffs
- KMS/HSM and audit evidence needs
- Throughput/latency benchmarking and token forecast
- Rollout timeline and gating criteria

Action items (recap): see action_items field above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I think we've got 45 minutes, we want to run through the extension ask, the EU on-prem pilot details, and then technical next steps. Priya, thanks for joining.
[00:16] Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks Alex, yeah appreciate it. Quick heads up, our board is looking for an answer on the contract terms by end of May, so timebox is tight.
[00:28] Marcus Lee: And from ops, we need the throughput guarantees — last cycle we saw some queuing during peak ingest, want to make sure the uplift addresses that.
[00:37] Samantha Green: Totally. We looked at your token profile Marcus, and initial recommendation was a dedicated pool with burst to hosted for weekend spikes. That gives predictable p99 but you still get elasticity.
[00:50] Marcus Lee: Dedicated pool is fine but curious about a hybrid for EU — we need data to stay in EU for PHI-ish workloads.
[00:57] Ellen Park: Yeah that's the compliance ask, we need KMS controls and audit log retention at 3 years. Also want to confirm whether Redwood can support customer-managed keys or if HSM is required.
[01:12] Alex Chen: Good notes. Ellen, Redwood supports both: we have our managed KMS and we also integrate with customer KMS (CloudKMS, Azure Key Vault). For HSM-backed keys we can do an enterprise add-on — I'll put the exact language in the amendment.
[01:28] Dr. Priya Rao: When you say integrate with customer KMS, is that full envelope encryption or are keys stored on Redwood? I've seen wording where keys are escrowed, want to avoid that.
[01:40] Samantha Green: The common pattern is we do envelope encryption, customer KMS holds the root keys, Redwood never has plain-text root keys. There was a doc — Sam-el integration? sorry — SAML earlier for SSO. But for KMS it's customer-controlled.
[01:56] Ellen Park: Ok can you send the SOC2 artifacts and the KMS flow diagram? We'll need to present to our security council.
[02:05] Alex Chen: Absolutely. I'll attach the SOC2 cert, the KMS architecture, and the audit log retention policy. I'll also propose contract language that explicitly says keys remain customer-managed and that logs are retained per your spec.
[02:18] Marcus Lee: On latency, target is p95 < 300ms for our clinical scoring model at median seq length; at 512 tokens it's more like p95 target 500ms but prefer as low as possible.
[02:30] Samantha Green: Right. For the model family you shared, we recommended a quantized instance on T4-class for EU on-prem pilot to balance cost and latency. For hosted we can use a higher perf instance. The tradeoff is cost versus headroom.
[02:48] Dr. Priya Rao: Can we see numbers? rough RPS to latency mapping?
[02:53] Samantha Green: Yes — I'll run two benchmark profiles: 1) throughput-focused (sustained 200 rps with batching) and 2) latency SLO (single-request cold/warm p95). I'll log token cost and tail latency.
[03:07] Marcus Lee: Great. Also need guidance on KV cache behavior — our app does lots of prefix reuse, so caching will matter for cost.
[03:16] Samantha Green: We'll capture prefix/KV cache hit rates in the benchmark runs. Note sometimes the transcript generator hears KV as "KV cash" so in the docs it's KV cache.
[03:25] Alex Chen: Ha, good note. On contract structure: Novaflow wants 12 months with a 20% uplift on current committed units and EU + APAC add-ons. We can sketch that as a base commitment plus reserved EU nodes for the on-prem pilot for 3 months.
[03:42] Dr. Priya Rao: For the EU on-prem pilot, are we having Redwood install the control plane or is this a customer-managed private deployment? Our security team prefers customer-managed with Redwood's slim agent.
[03:53] Samantha Green: We have a "Private Lite" pattern — customer manages infra, we provide an OVA/containerized runtime and a control connector. It keeps most telemetry minimal and provides audit hooks.
[04:05] Ellen Park: That sounds promising. What about patches and kernel updates? We need a patching SLA for the pilot.
[04:12] Samantha Green: We recommend a shared patching cadence: customer patches infra, Redwood pushes runtime updates, and we automate the runtime patching window with a maintenance SLA. We'll detail the patch window in the pilot README.
[04:25] Marcus Lee: Bandwidth/egress costs are also a thing. If inference happens in EU on-prem, what traffic still egresses?
[04:33] Samantha Green: Only control plane telemetry and aggregated anonymized metrics. Model weights and inference stay on-prem. We'll enumerate exact flows in the diagram.
[04:41] Dr. Priya Rao: Okay — on pricing, we need line items for dedicated EU nodes, pilot support hours, and the HSM add-on as optional.
[04:49] Alex Chen: I'll include those in the updated price sheet. We'll provide three tiers: pilot-only (3 months), pilot-to-prod (scale incremental), and committed multi-region (12 months).
[04:59] Marcus Lee: How does failover work if EU capacity is exhausted? Can we fallback to hosted EU region or to US?
[05:08] Samantha Green: We support policy-based routing. For EU-only regulated calls we recommend strict routing (no fallback). For less-sensitive traffic, policy can allow fallback to hosted EU; US fallback is last resort and requires consent in contract.
[05:22] Ellen Park: We'll probably restrict fallback for PHI. For non-PHI we may allow cross-border fallback with encryption in transit.
[05:30] Dr. Priya Rao: Timeline constraint — we want pilot live by start of Q3. Is that feasible?
[05:36] Samantha Green: If we get contract signed by end of May and we have your infra prep done in June, a July pilot start is doable. The gating items are keys and SOC2 doc sign-off and the benchmark pass.
[05:48] Alex Chen: Let's lock that. I'll circulate a timeline: contract redline in 24–48 hours, pricing sheet today, benchmarks provision week after, pilot kickoff in early July.
[06:00] Marcus Lee: On benchmarks, what metrics will you report? I want p50/p95/p99, token cost, CPU/GPU utilization, and cache hit rates.
[06:09] Samantha Green: We'll include those plus KV cache hit rate, inferred tokenization variance, and disk I/O for on-prem nodes. We'll also capture cold-start vs warm p95.
[06:20] Dr. Priya Rao: One more question: any known limits on model quantization? Our models rely on some ops that are finicky in lower-bit quant.
[06:28] Samantha Green: We'll note any operator mismatches in the benchmark results. If quantization causes regressions we'll propose hybrid: quantize non-critical layers or use mixed precision.
[06:37] Alex Chen: Competitors — you mentioned evaluating CumulusAI last quarter. Anything in their approach that swayed you?
[06:44] Dr. Priya Rao: Cumulus gave a lower sticker price but the integration story for customer KMS was weak. We'd prefer Redwood if keys and audit are clear.
[06:55] Ellen Park: Also BigCloudML was pitching global edge nodes but their SLA didn't cover audit logs retention.
[07:03] Samantha Green: Good context, will make sure our contract and annex reflect those audit requirements and KMS flow.
[07:10] Alex Chen: Ok, let's walk through the exact next steps again quickly. I'll send the amended contract and price sheet; Samantha will run the benchmarks; Ellen will confirm KMS/HSM; Marcus will provide forecast. We'll reconvene the week of 6/4.
[07:25] Dr. Priya Rao: Sounds good. One last nit — can Redwood mark redlines in the contract with rationale bullets? Makes the security review faster.
[07:33] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll include rationale comments inline.
[07:36] Marcus Lee: Thanks all.
[07:38] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via CRM and calendar invite for the 6/4 readout.
[07:45] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution (Speaker 2 labeled as "Speaker 1" early), minor mishearings ("KV cash" -> KV cache), acronyms sometimes separated (S A M L -> SAML).
